cards.back: **Data** = raw, unorganised facts. **Information** = data processed/organised/given context to be useful. *Information depends on data; data does not depend on information.*

**Database** = a logically-coherent collection of *related* data about a mini-world (UoD). **DBMS** = software that **defines, constructs, manipulates & shares** databases. (Catalog stores **metadata**.)
**Defining** (types/structures/constraints → metadata), **Constructing** (store data), **Manipulating** (query/update/report), **Sharing** (concurrent multi-user access).

① redundancy & inconsistency ② difficulty accessing data ③ data isolation ④ integrity problems ⑤ **atomicity** problems ⑥ concurrent-access anomalies ⑦ security problems. Each = a *purpose of a DBMS*.
**Entity** (unique ID), **Referential** (FK refers to existing PK), **Domain** (valid value range), **User-defined** (business rules).
**OLTP** = many users, small frequent retrievals/updates (banking, airlines). **OLAP** = analytical processing for decisions/predictive models, uses **data mining** (AI + statistics).
**Physical/internal** (how stored) → **Logical/conceptual** (what data + relationships) → **View/external** (part a user sees). Lowest = physical, highest = view.
**Physical** = change storage/indexes without changing the logical schema. **Logical** = change the logical schema without affecting applications (**harder** to achieve).
**Schema** = the design (≈ variable declarations); changes rarely. **Instance/state/snapshot** = the data at a moment (≈ variable values); changes often. Many states per schema.
**External** (user views) ↔ **Conceptual** (logical) ↔ **Internal** (physical storage). The mappings give logical (ext↔conc) and physical (conc↔int) data independence.
**Requirements** → **Conceptual** (ER model) → **Logical** (relational + normalization) → **Physical** (indexes/storage). Abstract → concrete.
**2-tier:** Client (UI) ↔ Server (DB) via ODBC/JDBC. **3-tier:** Client ↔ App/Web server (business logic) ↔ DB server — common for web, **more secure** (clients can't reach the DB directly).
**Naïve/parametric** (canned interface, e.g. ticket booking), **Application programmers** (back-end), **Sophisticated** (write own SQL), **DBA** (schema, access, backup/recovery).
**Centralized** (one server), **Client-server**, **Parallel** (cluster, analytics), **Distributed** (multi-location: scalable, fault-tolerant via replication).

A **conceptual** modeling technique; ER diagrams show **entities/attributes/relationships**. **Entity** = a distinct object; **entity set** = entities of the same type; **extension** = the actual collection.
**Simple** (ellipse), **Composite** (sub-parts), **Multivalued** (**double ellipse**), **Derived** (**dashed ellipse**), **Key** (**underlined**), Complex (composite+multivalued nesting).
**Descriptive attribute** = an attribute of a *relationship* (e.g. `grade` on `enrolls`), not an entity. **Null** = not applicable / missing / unknown.
**Relationship** = association among entities (diamond). **Degree** = # participating entity sets (binary=2, ternary=3). **Recursive** = same entity set participates twice (needs **role names**).
**1:1**, **1:N**, **N:1**, **M:N** — how many of B one A can relate to. e.g. works_for = 1:N (dept→employees); works_on = M:N (employee↔project).
**Total** = every entity must participate (**double line**); **Partial** = some may not (single line). Independent of cardinality (how-many vs whether-all).
Line carries **(l, h)**: l = minimum, h = maximum. **l=1 ⇒ total participation**; h=1 ⇒ at most one; h=N ⇒ no limit. (2,5) = between 2 and 5 relationships.
**Superkey** = uniquely identifies (may have extras). **Candidate key** = minimal superkey. **Primary key** = the chosen candidate key.
**1:1** → PK of either entity. **1:N/N:1** → PK of the **many side**. **M:N** → **union** of both PKs. (Descriptive attrs like grade are NOT in the PK.)

Existence-dependent on an **identifying (owner) entity**; **no PK of its own** → PK = owner PK + **discriminator**. Identifying relationship is **many-to-one + total participation**, no descriptive attrs.
Weak entity = **double rectangle**; identifying relationship = **double diamond**; discriminator (partial key) = **dashed underline**.
**Strong entity** → table, PK = entity PK. **Weak entity** → table with owner's PK; PK = owner PK + discriminator.
**1:N → foreign key on the many side.** **M:N → a new junction table** (both PKs as composite PK + relationship attrs). 1:1 → FK on either side.
**Composite** → flatten to leaf columns. **Derived** → not stored. **Multivalued** → its own table (attr + entity PK), to satisfy **1NF**.
**Procedural**, **closed** (every result is a relation → composable). Unary: **σ select, ∏ project, ρ rename**. Binary: **∪ ∩ − × ⋈ ÷**.
**σ_p(r)** = filter **rows** by predicate p (horizontal). **∏_{cols}(r)** = keep **columns** + **remove duplicates** (vertical). |result| ≤ |R| for both.
**ρ** renames a relation and/or attributes (needed for set ops & self-joins): ρ_{Old→New}(R). **←** names an intermediate result (step-by-step query).
Required for ∪, ∩, −: **(1) same arity** (# attributes) **(2) compatible domains** (matching column types).
**∪ and ∩** are commutative **and** associative. **Set difference is NOT commutative** (R−S ≠ S−R). And r∩s = r−(r−s).
**R(Z) ÷ S(X)** returns tuples of R (on Y=Z−X) that pair with **every** tuple of S. *Sailors who reserved **every** boat* = (∏sid,bid Reserves) ÷ (∏bid Boats).
Every tuple of R × every tuple of S. **Degree = n+m, size = |R|·|S|.** Usually meaningless until filtered by a selection (σ on matching keys).
Cartesian product **+ select on common-named compatible columns + drop the duplicate column**. The everyday way to follow a foreign key without cross-product redundancy.
**ℱ**: SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN, COUNT. Grouping attribute on the **left** of ℱ, aggregates on the right: `rating ℱ AVG(age)(Sailors)` = SQL **GROUP BY**.
**Select rows (σ) → join tables (⋈) → project columns (∏).** 'every/all' → **division**; 'not/without' → **set difference**; 'total/avg per' → **ℱ + grouping**.
SQL = ex-**SEQUEL** (Chamberlin & Boyce, IBM). **DDL** (CREATE/ALTER/DROP), **DML** (INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE), **DCL** (GRANT/REVOKE), **TCL** (COMMIT/ROLLBACK).

cards.front: CHAR vs VARCHAR; BLOB vs CLOB
cards.back: **CHAR(n)** = fixed length (pads spaces); **VARCHAR(n)** = variable. **BLOB** = binary LOB (images/video); **CLOB** = character LOB (text). DATE = `YYYY-MM-DD`.
**DROP** = removes data **+ structure** (DDL). **TRUNCATE** = removes all rows, **keeps structure** (DDL, resets AUTO_INCREMENT). **DELETE** = removes rows, **WHERE-filterable**, undoable (DML).
Changes table **structure**: `ADD` / `MODIFY` / `DROP COLUMN` / `RENAME COLUMN`, and add/drop constraints. (`CREATE…AS SELECT` copies structure+data; `CREATE…LIKE` copies structure only.)
**Key** (PK not duplicated), **Entity integrity** (PK not NULL), **Referential integrity** (FK matches an existing PK or is NULL).
**PRIMARY KEY** = UNIQUE **+** NOT NULL, only one per table. **UNIQUE** = a candidate/alternate key, allows one NULL.
On parent DELETE/UPDATE: **NO ACTION** (reject, default), **CASCADE** (propagate), **SET NULL** (FK→NULL, must be nullable), **SET DEFAULT** (FK→default).
**SELECT** clause = ∏ (project, columns); **FROM** = relation(s)/joins; **WHERE** = σ (select, rows). `SELECT name FROM r WHERE p` ≡ ∏name(σp(r)).
**INSERT INTO … VALUES** / **INSERT … SELECT** · **SELECT … FROM … WHERE** · **UPDATE … SET … WHERE** · **DELETE FROM … WHERE** (no WHERE → all rows!).

cards.front: SQL keyword SELECT vs algebra σ
cards.back: Beware: SQL's **`SELECT`** keyword does **projection (∏, columns)**; relational algebra's **`σ` select** picks **rows** — that's SQL's **`WHERE`**. Opposite meanings!

**1)** new bridge table for the relationship. **2)** both entities' PKs become FKs whose **combination is the composite PK**. **3)** relationship attributes (e.g. Date_of_assignment) move into the bridge table. e.g. `Advisor(Instructor_ID, Student_ID, Date_of_assignment)`.

cards.front: ALTER TABLE — add FK & MODIFY vs CHANGE
cards.back: Add FK: `ALTER TABLE t ADD CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY(col) REFERENCES p(col)` (column must exist). **MODIFY** col newtype = retype only; **CHANGE** old new type = rename **and** retype. `AFTER col`/`FIRST` set position.
